lesson: [qwen3.5_9b] Seed-subspace growth produced selective clusters of 64 to 2048 units. Recipe: take 3-14 attribution seeds in one layer, score every unit by how much its down column and gate/up rows project onto the seeds' span, subtract the same score for other skills' seed sets, and take the top K. Results: L31 capital_city .528 at 20 units, .588 at 64, .332 at 2048 (random same-size parts at most .052); L20 past_tense .23-.25 from 128 to 2048 units; L30 weekday .224 at 128 and 1024 (month barely moves); L26 colour .187 at 256.

[qwen3.5_9b] A 1.5x penalty on the other skills' subspaces (instead of 1x) fixed leaks at large K. With 1x, the L31 ordinal cluster at 256 units leaked weekday .176; with 1.5x it gave ordinal .39 with weekday .079, and still .40 at 1024. Capital at 512 went from facts leak .116 to .037. Attribution handles cap at 20 units, so weight-based growth is the only way to build large parts.

[qwen3.5_9b] Logit-lens writer clusters were not causal. The 64 L31/L30 columns most aligned with capital, colour, roman or month unembeddings dropped their skill by at most .07, often negative (colour -.129, month -.099). Under SwiGLU an activation's sign can flip, so a down column's direction alone is ambiguous. Use attribution seeds, then grow from the weights.

[qwen3.5_9b] Whole blocks, sublayers and head groups were never selective. Whole-MLP ablation at L24/L25/L27 dropped facts .32-.40 but month, colour or weekday by .11-.20. L23 full-attention heads 8-11 dropped facts .18 but past/ordinal by .07. L18 ordinal heads 0/4/14/19 gave .172 but moved controls by .06-.10. In o_proj, heads are nearly orthogonal (subspace overlap .004-.04), so heads can't be grown into groups by weight similarity.

[qwen3.5_9b] Clusters saturate. Mid-layer clusters (L12-L21) plateaued at .10-.148 even at 512-1024 units. Roman numerals stayed at ~.11, month at .13 and code at .10, and plurals, math and multilingual never exceeded .03. At 2048-4096 units, random same-size parts dropped weekday/colour by up to .23, so those screens failed. Clusters near .15-.17 often failed held-out: L26 weekday .153, L2 facts .171 at 256 units (the 128-unit version passed at .19).

[qwen3.5_9b] Weekday and month successor share one circuit, so neither can be screened alone. L19 full-attention heads 8-15 dropped weekday .381 and month .341; heads 12-15 gave .261/.154; an L12 MLP cluster grown from units 1877/6590 gave .169/.084; L23 head group 0 gave .186/.15. Attribution-based head swaps never separated them. Plan a combined calendar-successor skill before spending the skill cap.

[qwen3.5_9b] Logit-lens roman writers were real but too weak. L26 unit 4058 writes XX/XXX/XI/XII and L28 unit 480 writes VI/IV/IX. A 128-unit cluster grown from 4058 was clean: roman .127, other skills at most .019, random parts at most .001. It still failed the .15 bar and held-out. Growing it to 256-1024 units stayed around .12, so the support is split across layers and adding units at one layer does not help.

[qwen3.5_9b] Ordinal and colour heads are fragile to random head ablation, so their high target drops do not pass. L23 heads [0,5,9,12] cut ordinal .467, but the control moved .217 and random 4-head sets in that layer reached .446. L30 linear-attention colour heads [8,9,12,13] gave .157 but leaked into calendar and ordinal skills (.11-.17).

[qwen3.5_9b] Recipes that were inert here: unembedding-subspace ranking with a 1.5x penalty for month, plural and roman at L24-31 (at most .05); clusters grown from plural singular↔plural units L28 u3443 and L29 u3391 (about 0); multilingual clusters grown at L12/L16 (about 0); an L31 digit-writer cluster ranked by |cos| (math .007, and it raised calendar and ordinal scores by .1-.28). Math and code attribution was near zero at every layer scanned.

[qwen3.5_9b] Structure notes: full attention runs only at L3, 7, ..., 31 (16 heads, 4 KV groups, head_dim 256); the other layers are GatedDeltaNet with 32 value heads that share key heads in pairs. Bisecting by KV group found the calendar heads cheaply. Ablate handles are lowercased, so save /work JSON files with lowercase names.

[qwen3.5_9b] Projecting MLP columns onto the month unembedding subspace (minus 1.5x the best other category) picked month suppressors, not month writers. Ablating the top-256 sets improved month_successor by .278 at L31 and .077 at L30, with controls flat, and the L28 set was inert (-.003). Check the sign of the down-projection against the output direction, not just the norm fraction, before using these sets as writer clusters.

[qwen3.5_9b] The L31 top-256 Roman-numeral subspace cluster left roman_numeral unchanged (.014) but cut ordinal_words .302 (weekday .067, ordinal control .064). The output-token category does not tell you which skill a cluster serves, so ablate it against every skill before naming it.

[qwen3.5_9b] Ordinal_words at L31 is too diffuse for 256-unit MLP parts to pass the random gate. One of 5 random 256-unit L31 sets dropped it .35, more than the weight-picked cluster's .302. Unless the target drop is well above .35, don't screen ordinal at L31 with sets this size. Try earlier layers or smaller seed-grown clusters.

[qwen3.5_9b] The L31 plural-noun subspace cluster (256 units, top subspace score .56) was inert on plural_nouns (.024). A high subspace fraction alone did not predict a causal part for morphology skills at late layers. Plural is probably computed earlier, like past_tense at L20.

[general] With only about 7 minutes of wall clock, ablate 3-5 weight-scored candidates in parallel in the first minutes, then spend screens only on candidates with drop >.25. Skip the scan unlock path: it needs 5 run_python calls, which this budget cannot cover.
